input: Rust compiler project: struct Token { kind: TokenKind (enum, 40 variants), is_keyword: bool, start: u64, end: u64, line: u64, col: u64 } stored in Vec<Token>, ~10M tokens on a large workspace. Asked to make parsing faster.
expect: Probes size_of before touching anything; drops line/col/end as recomputable; start shrinks to u32 with the 4GB bound stated; is_keyword folds into TokenKind (encoding, not a field); lands near tag+offset (5-8 bytes); adds a const size assertion; reports the size table with N=10M totals measured.

input: Python ETL(extract-transform-load) job holds 5M row objects (class Row with 8 float attributes) in a list; resident memory exceeds 4GB. Asked to cut memory.
expect: Rejects field reordering as a non-move on boxed objects; applies slots as the cheap step and columnar (numpy/pyarrow/polars) as the real fix; measures with memray/tracemalloc or asizeof before and after; guard asserts the representation held; warns that a Python-level loop over the rows stays slow regardless.

input: Swift game: class Monster subclassed by 6 monster kinds, 50k live instances in an array, frame time spiky in the update loop.
expect: Replaces the class hierarchy with a struct/enum or tag+SoA encoding — no per-instance heap object or ARC traffic in the loop; measures MemoryLayout stride before/after; handles the alive flag out of band by partitioning; reports the size table.

input: User asks to apply data-oriented design to AppConfig — 30 fields, exactly one instance, loaded once at startup.
expect: Declines the shrink: N=1 means no footprint payoff; names what would qualify (a type with many live instances); changes no code.

input: Browser particle system in TypeScript: 200k particles as {x, y, vx, vy, alive, hue} objects in an array; GC pauses visible in traces.
expect: Moves to SoA with typed arrays (Float32Array per field); alive goes out of band via liveCount + swap-remove, not a boolean field; keeps shapes monomorphic; measures heap before/after; guards the representation in a test.

input: Rust AST: enum Node with 30 variants, largest variant 96 bytes, nodes own each other through Box<Node>, ~2M nodes for a big crate.
expect: Moves nodes into an arena Vec with u32 newtype indexes replacing Box pointers; replaces the max-size enum with the encoding approach (tag + common fields + repurposed operand + extra table) chosen from the observed variant distribution; measures average bytes per node before/after; adds size assertions on the common struct.
